planting.note: Root offsets or individual leaves in spring in lean, gritty, fast-draining succulent mix in full sun to bright light; as an old named hybrid it is propagated only vegetatively, not from seed.

directions: Grow in lean, gritty, well-drained succulent mix in full sun to bright light, letting the mix dry out fully between waterings. One of the oldest named echeveria hybrids still in cultivation, a cross between E. derenbergii and E. shaviana, it forms tight clustering rosettes of thick, frosted lavender-pink leaves with faintly ruffled, pink-tinged margins, combining the compact habit of one parent with the wavy leaf edge of the other. It offsets freely around the base to form slow-spreading clumps suited to troughs and rock garden crevices. Protect from hard frost and overhead watering, which can mar the delicate powdery leaf surface.

common_name: Mrs Giuseppi Hens and Chicks (Vintage British Hybrid Sempervivum)

planting.note: Plant offsets in spring or fall by pressing them onto the surface of very well-drained, sandy to gravelly, lean soil in full sun.

directions: Press offsets onto the surface of very well-drained, lean, gravelly soil in full sun, and divide congested mats every few years to keep rosettes vigorous. Mrs Giuseppi is one of the long-established British sempervivum hybrids still grown in alpine collections, forming small-to-medium rosettes with reddish-bronze tips over green bases that deepen in color through a cold winter. Like other classic UK-raised cultivars of its era it is a tough, reliable garden plant rather than a novelty form, spreading steadily by offsets to fill troughs and rock garden crevices. Sharp drainage and full sun are essential, since wet soil in winter is the most common cause of rot.

common_name: Variegated Ghost Plant (Cream-Marbled Mother of Pearl Plant)

planting.note: Root stem cuttings in spring in very well-drained, lean, gritty succulent mix in full sun to part shade; variegated sections are unstable from leaf cuttings, so stem cuttings that retain the growing tip hold the pattern more reliably.

directions: Grow in very well-drained, lean, gritty succulent mix in full sun to part shade, allowing the mix to dry out fully between waterings. This sought-after sport of the species carries irregular cream-to-white marbling across its pale blue-lavender, triangular leaves, giving each trailing rosette a mottled, painterly look that is more pronounced in bright light and cooler weather. Growth habit matches the plain species, with trailing stems that root readily where they touch soil, though variegated growth is generally slower and less vigorous. Watch for all-green reversion shoots and remove them promptly to keep the variegation from being overtaken.
